subject: Aerodyne RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing, SKU alignment & burst plan
messages:
From: Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@aerodyne.ai>

Cc: procurement@aerodyne.ai, Maya Patel <maya.patel@aerodyne.ai>

Subject: Aerodyne RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing and SKU alignment

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking our RFP — attached is Aerodyne's initial RFP workbook (Aerodyne_Dedicated_RFP_v1.xlsx). The core ask: we need a proposal for a reserved/dedicated pool that meets our projected 95th percentile sustained throughput of ~120M tokens/day with peak bursts up to 2.5x sustained for up to 3 hours/day.

Questions we want explicitly addressed in your response:
- Recommended GPU family mix (we currently evaluate H100 / A100-80GB / L4 options) and the rationale by workload shape.
- Expected sustained QPS / tokens-per-second per slot and expected tail latency at 99th pct for chat-style requests (avg sequence length ~512 tokens).
- Reservation sizing options (phased vs all-up) and recommended overprovision (% buffer) for 2.5x burst tolerance.
- Any pricing/commitment tiers that materially affect the recommended SKU mix.

We included a small sample of daytime workload traces in workbook tab 'sample' — if you need raw traces I can share. Please confirm a target date to return the completed sizing questionnaire.

Thanks,
Sarah Connors
Head of Procurement
Aerodyne Analytics

Hi Sarah — thanks for the workbook and clear asks. We're assigning a small cross-functional team to this (cc'd: Jonas, Karthik) and we'll return a completed sizing questionnaire plus a short, scenario-based proposal.

Attached: redwood_dedicated_sizing_questionnaire_v2.pdf — it mirrors your workbook but captures runtime assumptions we use for slot packing and tail-latency budgeting. A couple quick clarifications that will help us:
- The 120M tokens/day — is that tokenized per your internal tokenizer or BPE tokens aligned with GPT-style tokenization?
- For "chat-style requests" — please confirm what fraction are single-turn vs multi-turn (we'll assume 60% multi-turn with an average 4 turns unless you specify otherwise).

Proposed timeline: we can deliver an initial sizing + SKU mix by 2026-04-14. If that works, we can schedule a 60-min sizing workshop the week of 4/19 to align on tail-latency SLAs and the phasing approach.

Best,

- Multi-turn: current traffic is ~55% multi-turn, average 3.8 turns. We're expecting multi-turn ratio to grow to ~65% over next 6 months.

One more ask: how would you recommend we think about "slotting" for inference pools where we need predictable per-tenant latency but want to maximize packing? We worry about noisy neighbors during bursts.

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Aerodyne RFP: Dedicated capacity sizing and SKU alignment

Hi Sarah — looping in a short technical note to address slotting, GPU mix, and throughput assumptions (replying-all).

On Mon, Apr 13, 2026 at 08:47 AM Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@aerodyne.ai> wrote:
> One more ask: how would you recommend we think about "slotting" for inference pools where we need predictable per-tenant latency but want to maximize packing? We worry about noisy neighbors during bursts.

Short answer: hybrid reservation with soft burst lanes + per-tenant QoS. Details below.

1) Recommended GPU family mix (based on your trace shape: median seq ~256, 95th ~820):
   - H100 (FP8/FP16 friendly) x 20% of pool: use for high-throughput, low-latency critical tenants — best for heavy multi-turn dense contexts.
   - A100 80GB x 50% of pool: best general-purpose for long context (512-1024), good tradeoff for throughput and memory for your current mix.
   - L4 (or equivalent inference-optimized T4-class) x 30%: cost-efficient for short-turn, bursty Assist workloads and embedding-only flows.

2) Throughput and slot sizing (approximate):
   - A single A100-80GB slot (as we define it: 1 inference instance with moderate batching) ~ 80-120 tokens/sec for chat (512 avg) at p99 tail ~120-200ms depending on batching and KV-cache warm state.
   - H100 slot ~ 140-220 tokens/sec; p99 tail ~90-150ms.
   - L4 slot ~ 18-35 tokens/sec; p99 tail higher (~300-600ms) but much cheaper per token.

3) Burst tolerance & overprovision guidance:
   - For 2.5x peak bursts, plan: reserved baseline = sustained demand + 15% buffer. Then provide a soft-burst lane sized to handle the remaining burst capacity (approx 2.5x - 1.15x = 1.35x of sustained) via either (a) short-term on-demand capacity (our hosted pool) or (b) pre-allocated burst VMs in Dedicated with a fast auto-scale trigger.
   - Operationally, we recommend targeting 20-25% of total pool as burst-capable nodes that are allowed to oversubscribe to lower-priority tenants under normal conditions and can be preempted for critical tenants during configured SLO windows.

4) Slotting / noisy neighbor controls:
   - Per-tenant QoS: reserve tokens-per-second guarantees at the serving-layer; implement KV cache pinning for priority tenants to avoid cache-thrashing during bursts.
   - SLO-backed fallback: canary lower-quality model variant or quantized profile if tail-latency spikes and reserved burst capacity is exhausted.

5) Pricing/commitment notes (high-level):
   - Larger committed blocks (12+ months) materially lower per-token pricing on A100/H100 families. L4 pricing is much flatter and typically suited to variable traffic.

If helpful, we can map your 120M tokens/day target to concrete slot counts in the questionnaire and provide three phasing options: conservative (minimal upfront commit), balanced (recommended starting point), and aggressive (optimize for lowest unit cost). Tessa will follow up with the delivery that includes the workbook.

- Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
